scope: How work is broken into tasks for any delivery team: what makes a task specific and actionable, how large a task may be, one owner (assignee), a priority or order, acceptance or done criteria, the link from each task to its milestone, and how a blocked task names what it waits on. Out of scope: writing the spec before code (spec-driven-development), ordering thin end-to-end slices (steel-thread-first), milestones themselves (milestone-scheduling) and the general record-linking convention (project-record-linking); projectteam's own paths, formats and specialist names.
research_type: How-to / troubleshooting (intent Do; domain work decomposition and task assignment; method standards bodies and practitioner sources). Product / how-to bar LOW-MEDIUM (broad independent consensus), no escalation. No task-size claim found rests on a study or survey, so none was scored on the Statistical bar.

questions.text: Best practices: what is current best practice for this topic?
Known solutions: what solutions, patterns, libraries and tools already exist, and how do they compare?
Platform guidelines: what do the platform owners' own guidelines say, for each platform the topic touches (Apple, Android, Windows, web, the databases and runtimes concerned)?
The expert's view: if we hired an expert consultant in this topic, what would they tell us: what to do, what to avoid, and what people usually get wrong?

methodology.method: guidelines/researching/process/research-methodology-and-sources: orient and classify (how-to, work decomposition), go to the method owners and standards bodies first (Scrum Guide, Kanban Guide, PMI/PMBOK, ISO 21502, AXELOS PRINCE2, SAFe, NASA WBS Handbook, GAO Schedule Assessment Guide) and the trackers' own documentation (GitHub Issues, Jira, Linear), then practitioner sources (Wake, Cohn, Spolsky, Humanizing Work, Leopold and Magennis, DORA, GTD) for what no primary source covers; corroborate across independent publishers; record provenance at generation time.
methodology.search_strategy: WebSearch for each method owner's and tracker's guidance on decomposition, task size, assignment, priority, done criteria, milestones and blocked work; WebFetch of every cited page; every quote then re-checked verbatim against the page's own text fetched separately (whitespace and typographic quotes normalised).
methodology.inclusion: Method owners' guides, standards bodies' public pages and handbooks, trackers' own documentation, named practitioner articles with an author and a date where given.
methodology.exclusion: Community forum answers, marketplace app pages, AI content-farm pages, and any page whose quoted words could not be found in its fetched text. PMI (pmi.org), ISO (iso.org) and GAO (gaoinnovations.gov, gao.gov) refused automated fetches (HTTP 403), so no claim cites them.
methodology.scoring: guidelines/researching/evidence/verification-and-trust-scoring: Authority (30) + Independent corroboration (25) + Accuracy/verifiability (20) + Currency (10) + Transparency (15), capped by the how-to domain ceiling; cite-the-claim-not-the-document, independence-before-corroboration, domain-stratified-trust, suppress-unsupported-confidence and provenance-at-generation-time applied; secondary sources standing in for an unreachable primary are scored down and say so.

summary: The four Worker Focus clauses hold at SHOULD: the Scrum Guide has Developers decompose items into work items of one day or less and own their plan; the NASA WBS Handbook ties work to responsibility (RAM) and derives tasks and milestones from the WBS; Wake's SMART tasks, Linear's method and GTD's next action make a task specific and actionable with a done test; the Kanban Guide requires blocked work to be actively unblocked, the Scrum Guide has the Daily Scrum identify impediments, and GitHub, Jira and Linear all record blocked-by relations. Of the three Verify clauses, 'every todo has an assignee and priority' is contradicted as a check on every todo: Cohn and Scrum.org advise against assigning all tasks up front, the Scrum Guide orders the backlog rather than labelling priority, and Linear's priority includes 'No priority'; the sources support one owner per started task and an ordered backlog. 'Blocked todos reference a specific blocker' is supported only at SHOULD (trackers provide the link, practitioners record the reason; no source requires it). 'No todo is assigned to a nonexistent milestone' has no source. New practices found: a task's text names the action and its done condition; tasks sized at hours to a few days with a week as the outer limit; a blocker recorded as a link to the blocking item plus a short reason and dates; one owner per started task, claimed when work begins; an ordered backlog; vertical rather than layer splits; decomposition covering 100% of scope; sizing by the people doing the work.
open_questions: Whether 'every todo has an assignee' should become 'every started todo has exactly one assignee', leaving unstarted todos unassigned as Cohn and Scrum.org advise, or stay a check on every todo as a projectteam convention; the owner decides.
Whether 'priority' is kept as a per-task field (as Linear and Jira offer) or replaced by backlog order (as the Scrum Guide has it), and whether 'no priority' is an allowed value.
Whether 'no todo is assigned to a nonexistent milestone' is kept as a house referential-integrity check; no external source states it, though trackers only offer existing milestones to pick.

Which task-size limit the guideline states: one day or less (Scrum Guide), hours to a couple of days with a week as too big (DORA), 2 to 16 hours (Spolsky), or 80 hours (WBS heuristic); the sources agree on 'small' but not on one number.
Whether a blocker must name a tracked item (a blocked-by link) or may name an outside cause in text (a vendor, a missing decision), and whether its start date is required.
Whether every task must link to a milestone, or only tasks in a project that uses milestones; the sources describe milestones as optional grouping.
limitations: PMI (the PMBOK Guide and the Practice Standard for Work Breakdown Structures), ISO 21502 and the GAO Schedule Assessment Guide could not be read: pmi.org, iso.org and gaoinnovations.gov/gao.gov refused automated fetches (HTTP 403). The WBS 100% rule and 80-hour heuristic are cited from Wikipedia's summary of the PMI practice standard, a secondary source, and the NASA WBS Handbook stands in as the primary WBS source.

AXELOS's PRINCE2 manual is paywalled and its own public summary could not be fetched as a document; the work package is cited from the PRINCE2 wiki (EMPII Group, using the trade mark under AXELOS permission), a secondary source.
ISO 31000 (risk) was not researched: blocked tasks are a flow concern here, not a risk-register one, and no risk-specific task rule is under verification.
LeSS was not cited: no LeSS page was found that speaks to task breakdown, assignment or blockers beyond what the Scrum Guide says.
Apple, Android and Windows have no bearing on this topic and were not researched.
No study or survey measuring the effect of a task-size limit on schedule accuracy was found; every size figure here is a method owner's or practitioner's heuristic, scored on the how-to bar.
Linear's documentation was reorganised; its former issue-relations and priority pages return 404, and those facts are cited from the current issue-property page.
No source was found that states a rule against assigning a task to a milestone that does not exist.
license: MIT (this research record); quoted material remains under its sources' terms and is quoted for verification.

claims.question: known-solutions
claims.claim: GitHub, Jira and Linear each record a blocker as a 'blocked by' / 'blocks' link from the blocked item to the item it waits on, and mark blocked items visibly.
claims.quote: Issue dependencies let you define issues that are blocked by, or blocking, other work. | Blocked issues are marked with a "Blocked" icon on your project boards or repository's Issues page | If there's a dependency between two work items, one must be finished before the next can begin. | Select either blocks or is blocked by, then select the work item to link. | If other issues are blocking the current issue, they'll show up in the issue sidebar with an orange flag under Blocked by.

citations.title: Create or remove dependencies on your timeline
citations.author: Atlassian

claims.query: GitHub issue dependencies blocked by; Jira blocks is blocked by; Linear blocked by relation

trust.basis: Three independent trackers' own current documentation converge on the same relation. Second check 2026-11-24: refuted (quote-found yes, supports-claim partly): The quote shows the "blocks / is blocked by" link in all three trackers, and visible marking only in GitHub (a "Blocked" icon) and Linear (an orange flag). The quoted Jira timeline text shows only how to make the link, not that blocked items are marked, so the claim that "each" marks blocked items visibly is not supported for Jira; lowered 85->65.

claims.question: known-solutions
claims.claim: Jira marks a blocked item with a flag (stored as 'Impediment') and lets the user add a comment giving the reason when flagging or unflagging it.
claims.quote: You can flag a work item to indicate that it's important or blocked. | You can also add a comment when you're adding a flag to or removing a flag from a work item. You may want to do this to indicate your reason for adding or removing the flag. | The flag for a work item is stored in a custom checkbox field called "Flagged", which has only one value: Impediment.
claims.query: Jira Cloud flag a work item impediment

trust.basis: The tracker's own current documentation; the reason comment is optional ('may want to').

claims.question: experts-view
claims.claim: Practitioners record each blocker on the blocked item with a brief reason that names its cause, and its start and resolved dates or days blocked, then keep resolved blockers to cluster them for improvement.
claims.quote: A common technique used by teams is to add a red Post-it note with a brief reason to the blocked work ticket. | Make sure each blocker has enough text to remind the team of the cause of the blocker | Some teams record the start date on the bottom left of the Post-it and the resolved date on the bottom right. | After you resolve these blockers, DON'T THROW THE BLOCKER POST-ITS AWAY!

citations.title: Using Blocker Clustering, Defect Clustering, and Prioritization for Process Improvement
citations.author: Klaus Leopold and Troy Magennis

claims.query: blocker clustering Klaus Leopold record blocker reason date

trust.basis: Named Kanban experts in an edited outlet; the reason practice is echoed by Jira's flag comment (claim jira-flag-with-reason), but the dates practice is 'some teams'.

claims.question: known-solutions
claims.claim: GTD keeps items that wait on someone or something else on a separate Waiting For list, naming what they wait on.
claims.quote: Waiting For holds those items that you are waiting on from someone or something else.
claims.query: GTD key definitions waiting for

trust.basis: Method owner's own page, but a personal-productivity method; shows a blocker can be a person or outside thing, not only a tracked item. Second check 2026-11-24: refuted (quote-found yes, supports-claim partly): The source says only that Waiting For holds items "you are waiting on from someone or something else" and gives examples (call backs, email replies, orders). It never says an entry should name the person or thing being waited on; lowered 55->35.
